chunks: 1935 - Abū Baṣīr narrated from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn."

He عليه السلام said: "It was revealed concerning Khawwāt ibn Jubayr al-Anṣārī. He was with the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in the trench while he was fasting, and he entered the evening in that state. Before this verse was revealed, when one of them slept, food became forbidden to him. So Khawwāt came to his family when evening came and said, 'Do you have any food?' They said, 'Do not sleep until we prepare food for you.' Then he reclined and fell asleep. They said, 'You have done it.' He said, 'Yes.' So he spent the night in that state and entered the morning. Then he went out to the trench, and he began to faint. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed by him, and when he saw what was with him, he informed him how his affair had been. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
"And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn."

key_terms.الْخَنْدَقِ: the trench, referring to the setting of the event
key_terms.الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ: the white thread, meaning the visible light of dawn in this context
key_terms.الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ: the black thread, meaning the darkness of night in contrast to dawn
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn, the point at which eating and drinking become forbidden for the fasting person
key_terms.حَرُمَ عَلَيْهِ الطَّعَامُ: food became forbidden to him, describing the earlier ruling before this verse
key_terms.صَائِمٌ: fasting; being in the state of sawm

ai.seo_question: Why was the verse 'And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn' revealed?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the occasion of revelation for the verse permitting eating and drinking during the night of fasting until true dawn becomes clear. It shows that an earlier hardship—food becoming forbidden after sleep—was lifted by this Quranic ruling. The report therefore clarifies the timing of imsak in sawm and situates the verse within a concrete historical event.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1935 - Abu Basir narrated from one of the Imams (as) regarding the verse of Allah (swt), the Exalted:
"And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187).

Imam (as) said: "This verse was revealed about Khawwat ibn Jubayr al-Ansari. He was with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) during the Battle of the Trench while fasting. Before this verse was revealed, if anyone slept at night, food became forbidden for them. Khawwat came to his family at night and asked: 'Do you have any food?' They said: 'Do not sleep until we prepare food for you.' He reclined and fell asleep. When they told him: 'You have already slept,' he replied, 'Yes, I did.' He remained in that state, fasting until the next day, and went to the trench, where he started to faint.
The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him, and when he saw his condition, he asked about his situation. Khawwat then explained what had happened. Then Allah (swt), the Exalted, revealed:
'And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn.'
